output.brief: The tripling of stops comes from the firmware 6.4 upgrade interacting with the new gloss stretch film. It isn't caused by the temps. Firmware 6.4 keeps weak short-range returns that 6.3 discarded, and the gloss film on staged pallets produces such returns at oblique angles. A bench test with no people present showed 17/20 stops for 6.4 with gloss film. The other three combinations gave 1/20, 0/20 and 0/20. Fleet data agrees. Upgraded pallet robots in Zones A/B rose from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 robot-hours, while the 6.3 robots working the same zones stayed flat at about 3.1 to 3.3. Tote robots in Zone C, where no wrapped pallets are staged, were unchanged. Nearly all the added stops had no person nearby, and temps were spread across all zones. I am fairly confident (about 85%). Next steps: switch back to the previous matte film, which restores normal rates without a firmware change, and track stops weekly by zone and firmware group. Roll the 30 pallet robots back to 6.3 only if the film can't be changed quickly. Don't adopt the three-strike policy or the shortened protective fields, because they would punish the wrong people and weaken safety. Test the December release against the gloss film before relying on it.
